summary: guest-manager's IntersectionObserver callback now filters entries through isSettledIntersection(): isIntersecting && boundingClientRect.top > 0, rejecting observe()'s initial-callback artifact before layout settles. Chose this over skip-first-callback (not an entry fact) and a scrollHeight gate (needs the ancestor scroller, which the sentinel exists to avoid). Documented beside the observer. Proven with 3 synthetic-entry unit tests, no forced race. Real scroll still loads the next page. e2e/layout: 6 consecutive clean full runs (40/40) after.

acceptance.criterion: The observer callback rejects an intersection that is an artifact of unsettled layout. The implementation is yours — skipping the first callback per observer instance, requiring the sentinel's boundingClientRect.top to be below the viewport top, or gating on the scroller having non-zero scrollHeight are all plausible. State which you chose and why the others were not
acceptance.evidence: src/app/screens/guest-manager/guest-manager.ts: new exported isSettledIntersection(entry) = entry.isIntersecting && entry.boundingClientRect.top > 0, used as entries.some(isSettledIntersection) in the constructor's IntersectionObserver callback (was entries.some(entry => entry.isIntersecting)). Chose boundingClientRect.top > 0 (the second listed option). Rejected skip-the-first-callback: it is state about the observer's call count, not a fact about one IntersectionObserverEntry, so it cannot be 'a pure predicate over an IntersectionObserverEntry' as the acceptance bullet itself requires two lines later, and it re-arms every time the constructor's effect() rebuilds the observer for a fresh ElementRef (viewChild swap), which happens on every re-entry to /guests — exactly when the race is live. Rejected the scrollHeight gate: it requires a reference to whichever ancestor actually scrolls, which is precisely the coupling the sentinel's own pre-existing doc comment (guest-manager.ts, scrollSentinel field) says this mechanism exists to avoid ('this screen never needs a reference to that element'); adding it back just to guard a callback reintroduces the fragility ADR-0043 already had to fix once (which ancestor scrolls changed between ADR-0042 and ADR-0043, and the sentinel design's whole point was not caring).

acceptance.criterion: Do not try to force the race to prove the fix. Instead make the guard a pure predicate over an IntersectionObserverEntry and unit-test it directly with synthetic entries — settled-and-intersecting, unsettled-and-intersecting, settled-and-not-intersecting
acceptance.evidence: isSettledIntersection() takes only Pick<IntersectionObserverEntry, 'isIntersecting' | 'boundingClientRect'> and touches no class/instance state — pure. guest-manager.spec.ts, new describe 'GuestManager — sentinel guard rejects an unsettled-layout intersection (T356)': 3 tests with synthetic entries — entry(true, 480) => true (settled-and-intersecting), entry(true, 0) => false (unsettled-and-intersecting, the initial-callback artifact), entry(false, 2400) => false (settled-and-not-intersecting). `npx ng test --watch=false --include='src/app/screens/guest-manager/guest-manager.spec.ts'` -> 'Test Files 1 passed (1)', 'Tests 49 passed (49)' (46 pre-existing + these 3). risks.risk: isSettledIntersection() rejects an entry whose boundingClientRect.top is exactly <= 0, which includes the (very rare, self-correcting) case of a real scroll gesture landing the sentinel precisely at the viewport's top edge mid-scroll — that single frame's callback is dropped, but the sentinel is pinned after the last row, so it moves further down as soon as loadMore() actually succeeds and is re-observed on the very next intersection change regardless. Not observed in any of this session's test runs; noted because it is a real, if negligible, edge the predicate does not special-case.
risks.surfaces_at: milestones or seating-plan, if either adopts this exact predicate against a sentinel whose layout puts it near the viewport top rather than the bottom (this predicate's top > 0 reasoning assumes a bottom sentinel, per its own doc comment; a top-anchored 'load more at the top' pattern would need the inverse check).
